title_en: Century Securities Co., Ltd. v. Tianjin Housing Provident Fund Management Center, Century Securities Co., Ltd., Tianjin Century Avenue Business Department, China Tourism International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd., Tianjin Securities Trading Business Department, and China Tourism International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd. — tort dispute
ruling_gist_en: When a customer opens an account and invests with a securities company, the securities company and its business department bear both a contractual duty of proper custody and a statutory duty of proper custody over the funds and securities in the customer's account. If the securities company's business department misappropriates funds or securities in the customer's account, it constitutes both breach of contract and tort. The customer has the right to choose to hold the securities business department liable for breach of contract or for tort. If the customer brings a civil lawsuit against the securities business department on the grounds of tort, the people's court of the place where the tort was committed or the place where the defendant has its domicile shall have jurisdiction in accordance with Article 29 of the Civil Procedure Law.

full_text_en:
Century Securities Co., Ltd. v. Tianjin Housing Provident Fund Management Center, Century Securities Co., Ltd. Tianjin Century Avenue Business Department, China Travel International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd. Tianjin Securities Exchange Business Department, and China Travel International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Tort

【Ruling Summary】

Where a client opens an account and invests in a securities company, the securities company and its business departments are obligated not only to exercise due care in the safekeeping of funds and securities in the client's account as agreed in the contract, but also to exercise due care in the safekeeping thereof as required by law. Where a securities company's business department misappropriates funds or securities in a client's account, such conduct constitutes both a breach of contract and a tort. The client is entitled to choose to seek either contractual liability or tort liability from the securities business department. Where a client brings a civil action against a securities business department on grounds of tort, the court of the place where the tort was committed or the court of the defendant's domicile shall have jurisdiction, in accordance with the provisions of Article 29 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2005) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 207

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Century Securities Co., Ltd., domiciled at: 41st Floor, China Merchants Bank Building, No. 7088 Shennan Avenue, Shenzhen, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Duan Qiang, Chairperson of the Board of the Company.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Tianjin Housing Provident Fund Management Center, domiciled at: No. 8 Lasa Road, Heping District, Tianjin.

Legal Representative: Li Yuhan, Director of the Center.

Defendant at First Instance: Century Securities Co., Ltd. Tianjin Century Avenue Business Department, domiciled at: Third Floor, Agricultural Bank Building, No. 90 Century Avenue, Dagang District, Tianjin.

Defendant at First Instance: China Travel International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd. Tianjin Securities Exchange Business Department, domiciled at: Third Floor, Agricultural Bank Building, No. 90 Century Avenue, Dagang District, Tianjin.

Person in Charge: Xu Yingzi, Director of the Business Department.

Defendant at First Instance: China Travel International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd., domiciled at: No. 2 Xinzhong Street, Dongcheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Feng Zongsu, Chairperson of the Board of the Company.

The Appellant Century Securities Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Century Securities) appealed against the Civil Ruling (2005) Jin Gao Min Si Chu Zi No. 7-1 rendered by the Tianjin High People's Court regarding a tort dispute with the Appellee Tianjin Housing Provident Fund Management Center (hereinafter referred to as the Housing Provident Fund) and the Defendants at First Instance: Century Securities Co., Ltd. Tianjin Century Avenue Business Department (hereinafter referred to as Century Business Department), China Travel International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd. Tianjin Securities Exchange Business Department (hereinafter referred to as CTS Business Department), and China Travel International Trust and Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as CTS Trust). This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel composed of Presiding Judge Wu Qingbao, Acting Judges Jia Wei and Sha Ling to hear the case. The court clerk was Yuan Hongxia. The case is now closed.

The following facts were found: On July 2, 2004, the Housing Provident Fund opened a funds account with the CTS Business Department, account number 81000066. On the 8th of that month, the Housing Provident Fund instructed the CTS Business Department to purchase with RMB 74.2 million the national debt designated by code 010405, with a face value of RMB 78,949,000. In July 2005, the Housing Provident Fund was unable to access the funds account. After negotiations with the CTS Business Department, the statement of account showed that the national debt purchased by the Housing Provident Fund had been misappropriated.

At the beginning of 2002, Century Securities began the overall acquisition of the securities assets of CTS Trust. From May 1, 2002, Century Securities exercised the right of management. On September 29, 2003, CTS Trust and Century Securities entered into an agreement whereby all securities assets belonging to CTS Trust were transferred to Century Securities. On July 28, 2005, the CTS Business Department issued an explanation to the Housing Provident Fund, stating that its original headquarters was CTS Trust, and that from July 2002 the securities assets of the six business departments of the former CTS Trust had been substantially taken over by Century Securities, and that the CTS Business Department was then affiliated with Century Securities. On its promotional webpage, Century Securities publicized that the Century Business Department was established on the basis of the agreed acquisition of the CTS Business Department. On August 9, 2005, Century Securities issued an explanation to the Housing Provident Fund, acknowledging that it owed the Housing Provident Fund RMB 74.2 million for entrusted national debt funds, and discussed using relevant property as compensation for the debt. The CTS Business Department had already been renamed as the Century Business Department.

On July 28, 2005, the Housing Provident Fund filed an action with the court of first instance on the ground of tort dispute, requesting a judgment ordering the Century Business Department, Century Securities, the CTS Business Department, and CTS Trust to return to the Housing Provident Fund the national debt (04 National Debt (5) with code 010405) that had been purchased, or to compensate for corresponding losses. During the period for responding to the complaint at first instance, Century Securities raised an objection to jurisdiction.

The Tianjin High People's Court, upon review, held that: The Housing Provident Fund brought the action on the ground of tort. According to the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), an action brought on the basis of a tort dispute shall be under the jurisdiction of the court of the place where the tort was committed or the court of the defendant's domicile. Tianjin is the place where the tort was committed. The defendants in this case, the Century Business Department and the CTS Business Department, are both domiciled in Tianjin. Therefore, the Tianjin High People's Court has jurisdiction over this case. In accordance with the provisions of Article 38 of the Civil Procedure Law, the court rendered a ruling to dismiss the objection raised by Century Securities to the jurisdiction of this case.

Century Securities, dissatisfied with the Civil Ruling (2005) Jin Gao Min Si Chu Zi No. 7-1 of the Tianjin High People's Court, appealed to this Court, alleging: This case is a dispute arising from entrusted financial management, and the appellant did not commit any tort. The court of first instance erroneously used the "place where the tort was committed" as the criterion to determine the competent court. According to the Civil Procedure Law, the jurisdiction of this case should be determined solely by the "place of contract performance" or the "defendant's domicile". Both the "defendant's domicile" and the "place of contract performance" are in Shenzhen, Guangdong Province. Therefore, the Tianjin High People's Court has no jurisdiction over this case, and the case should be transferred to the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court for jurisdiction.

The Housing Provident Fund responded: There is no contractual relationship between the Housing Provident Fund and Century Securities. The misappropriation of the Housing Provident Fund's national debt by Century Securities and the other defendants constitutes a tort. According to the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law that "an action arising from a tort shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the tort was committed or the place where the defendant is domiciled" and "where two or more people's courts have jurisdiction over an action, the plaintiff may file the action with one of those people's courts", there are four defendants in this case, of which two defendants, the Century Business Department and the CTS Business Department, are in Tianjin, and the act of misappropriating the national debt in this case occurred in Tianjin. The Housing Provident Fund is entitled to choose to file the action with the Tianjin High People's Court. Even if this case were, as the appellant claims, a contract dispute, because the Century Business Department and the CTS Business Department are in Tianjin and the place of contract performance is also in Tianjin, the Tianjin High People's Court would also have jurisdiction. The Housing Provident Fund requests that the second-instance court dismiss the appeal and affirm the original ruling.

This Court holds: Where a client opens an account and invests in a securities company business department, the securities company and its business departments are obligated not only to exercise due care in the safekeeping of funds and securities in the client's funds account as agreed in the contract, but also to exercise due care in the safekeeping thereof as required by law. Where the securities or funds in the client's account are misappropriated by the securities business department, according to Article 122 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "Where the breach of contract by one party infringes upon the personal or property interests of the other party, the injured party is entitled to choose to demand that the breaching party assume liability for breach of contract in accordance with this Law, or assume liability for tort in accordance with other laws", the client is entitled to choose either breach of contract or tort as the cause of action for bringing a civil lawsuit. In this case, because the national debt in the funds account of the Housing Provident Fund at the CTS Business Department was misappropriated, the Housing Provident Fund brought a civil action against the CTS Business Department and the other relevant defendants on the ground of tort in the Tianjin High People's Court, which is located where the CTS Business Department is domiciled. According to Article 29 of the Civil Procedure Law, which provides: "An action arising from a tort shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court of the place where the tort was committed or the place where the defendant is domiciled", the Tianjin High People's Court has jurisdiction over this case. Century Securities alleges on appeal that this case is a dispute arising from entrusted financial management, but fails to provide relevant evidence to support this. Its request to transfer this case to the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court, Guangdong Province, lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court will not support it. In accordance with Articles 29 and 154 of the Civil Procedure Law, this Court rules as follows:

The appeal is dismissed and the original ruling is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 50 shall be borne by Century Securities Co., Ltd.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Wu Qingbao
Acting Judge: Jia Wei
Acting Judge: Sha Ling

November 29, 2005
